positions.stakeholder_concern: The commenter finds the scope of what counts as "generative" AI ambiguous, questioning whether devices that derive insights from existing research fall within the definition, and notes that causal AI models operate differently from correlation-based approaches and are not clearly addressed.
positions.requested_fda_action: Provide a broader explanation of which AI-enabled devices are covered by the framework, or issue a parallel discussion paper addressing causal AI models.
positions.public_summary: Commenter seeks clarity on which AI-enabled devices count as "generative," including those deriving insights from existing research, and notes causal AI models work differently from correlation-based ones. Asks FDA to broaden the scope explanation or issue a companion paper on causal AI.
positions.source_passage: Generative AI is both very broad and very specific. Is it the FDA's stance that devices that derive information from existing research and generate insights be termed generative? Causal AI models approach the task in a very different way and have more power in healthcare in terms of causal versus correlation analysis. I would recommend either a broader explanation of the AI enabled devices, or to create a causal ai proposal mirroring this one.
